mainTopic: Moving tools and objects on שבת: tools used mainly for forbidden work, טלטול מן הצד, broken needles, and straightening a baby's limbs
overview: This amud opens with רבה's rule: a tool whose main job is forbidden work on שבת may still be moved for a permitted use of the tool itself (לצורך גופו). אביי challenges him from a מדוכה (mortar), and רבה answers that this source follows רבי נחמיה's strict view. אביי challenges again from an עלי (large pestle). רבה answers with רב's teaching that an owner who is careful about a tool gives it a fixed place, so everyone forbids moving it. Next, אמוראים argue over whether the משנה's nut-cracking hammer belongs to a goldsmith or a spice merchant. The גמרא then discusses food buried in straw or coals. רב נחמן rules like רבי אלעזר בן תדאי that it may be speared with a reed, because טלטול מן הצד is not real moving. רב נחמן's opposite ruling about a radish is explained as a ruling he took back. Then רב יוסף, אביי and רבא debate whether a needle missing its eye or point is still a כלי on שבת. Finally, a new מחלוקת begins about straightening a baby's limbs on שבת, and רב נחמן's proof for his view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A tool used mainly for forbidden work may be moved for a permitted use of the tool itself
steps.stepSummary: רבה's rule: a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved לצורך גופו.
steps.simpleTranslation: An object whose main use is forbidden on שבת may be moved when you need the object itself for a permitted purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states רבה's rule. A tool normally used for forbidden work, like a hammer, may be picked up on שבת if you want to use it for something permitted, like cracking nuts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a tool for forbidden work does not make the object totally off-limits. It still has the status of a כלי, and using it for a permitted job is allowed. This rule is the target of everything that follows next.

keyTerms.meaning: An object whose main function is a forbidden מלאכה
For the use of the object itself (for a permitted task)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved לצורך גופו.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the object is 'not מוקצה' in every way. It is still a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור. רבה only allows moving it for a permitted use of the object itself. Do not assume it may be moved for any reason at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This category, כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור לצורך גופו, is a basic rule of מוקצה and appears in הלכה למעשה.

phrases.english: An object whose function is for a prohibited use
for the purpose of the object itself — is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר שֶׁמְּלַאכְתּוֹ לְאִיסּוּר לְצוֹרֶךְ גּוּפוֹ מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the sugya from the previous daf, where רבה's position is being laid out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved on שבת לצורך גופו.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבה from the case of the mortar
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא: a מדוכה with garlic in it may be moved, and an empty one may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected to רבה: A mortar, if it has garlic in it, one may move it; if not, one may not move it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a source that seems to contradict רבה. An empty mortar may not be moved at all, even though someone could want it for a permitted use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מדוכה is a tool for crushing, which is forbidden work, so it is a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור. If רבה were right, an empty mortar could be moved for some permitted use of the mortar itself. The ברייתא forbids it completely and allows moving it only because of the garlic inside.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from a תנאי source)

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to Rabba:

phrases.aramaic: מְדוֹכָה, אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ שׁוּם — מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָהּ,
phrases.english: A mortar, if there is garlic in it — one may move it,
and if not — one may not move it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved לצורך גופו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An empty mortar is a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור, yet the ברייתא forbids moving it with no exception for a permitted use. This contradicts רבה.

steps.title: רבה answers that the source follows רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה, who allows a כלי to be moved only for its own designated use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: Whose view is this? It is רבי נחמיה, who says a vessel may be moved only for its designated use.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends himself. The mortar ברייתא follows a strict, minority opinion, so it does not disprove his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה holds that any כלי may be moved only for the job it was made for. An empty mortar's job is crushing, which is forbidden, so it cannot be moved at all. רבה does not rule like רבי נחמיה, so the ברייתא is no problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא with a very strict view on moving כלים on שבת
For the purpose of its designated use

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up לצורך גופו (רבה's term) with לצורך תשמישו (רבי נחמיה's term). לצורך גופו means any permitted use of the object. לצורך תשמישו means only the object's own designated job.

phrases.english: He said to him: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Nechemya,
who says: A vessel may not be moved
except for the purpose of its designated use.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a minority תנא (רבי נחמיה) whose view is not followed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mortar ברייתא reflects the accepted halacha and forbids moving a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור even for a permitted use.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה's strict view only, so רבה's rule stands.

steps.title: אביי challenges again from the pestle used to cut meat
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about cutting meat on an עלי. Both agree that after the cutting, it may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected again: בית שמאי say one may not take the pestle to cut meat on it, and בית הלל permit it. Yet all agree that once he has cut meat on it, it is forbidden to move it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second source against רבה. רבה's answer comes in steps 5 and 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עלי is a large pestle used for pounding grain, which is forbidden work. בית הלל let it be used to cut meat on יום טוב, which is a permitted use. Yet everyone agrees that once the cutting is done it may not be moved, so the עלי seems to be treated as off-limits.

keyTerms.meaning: A large pestle used for pounding grain
The two great schools of תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: The real attack is in the words 'וְשָׁוִין' (and all agree), not in the dispute itself. The dispute in parentheses is just background quoted from the משנה.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: (Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נוֹטְלִין אֶת הָעֱלִי לְקַצֵּב עָלָיו בָּשָׂר.
phrases.english: One may not take the pestle to cut meat on it.
phrases.notes: This is a יום טוב case, where cutting meat for the meal is needed.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel permit it.)
And they agree that if he cut meat on it,
it is forbidden to move it!
phrases.notes: The exclamation marks this as the point of the challenge against רבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים אֵין נוֹטְלִין אֶת הָעֱלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first objection was answered in step 3, אביי brings a new source against the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved לצורך גופו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The עלי is a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור. Everyone agrees it becomes forbidden to move once the meat is cut. This suggests that such a tool does not get a general permission, which goes against רבה.

steps.title: רבה first planned to answer like רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רבה's first idea was to answer the קשיא from the עלי by saying that this source follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה thought to answer him by saying this source follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how רבה first wanted to answer אביי's challenge from the עלי. This is only his first idea, and the next step tells us he changed his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3 רבה pushed away the מדוכה ברייתא by saying it follows רבי נחמיה. Here he considered using the same answer again for the עלי. The word סבר ("he thought") is a hint that this answer will be replaced.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought / he was planning to (often a first idea that gets replaced)
To answer / to resolve a difficulty
תנא who allows moving a כלי only for its own designated use

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT רבה's final answer. The word סבר tells you he only thought about saying it. His real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: He (Rabba) thought to answer him: it follows Rabbi Nechemya.
phrases.notes: The same move רבה used in step 3 for the מדוכה ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts רבה's response to the עלי challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a minority תנא (רבי נחמיה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עלי case contradicts רבה's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed only: the עלי source follows רבי נחמיה. This answer is then abandoned.

steps.title: רבה's real answer: a tool the owner is careful about gets a fixed place
steps.stepSummary: After hearing רב's teaching that everyone agrees about launderers' pins, presses and rods, רבה answered that the עלי also has a fixed place, so it may not be moved even according to his own rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But once he heard what רב חיננא בר שלמיא said in the name of רב: everyone agrees about launderers' pins, presses and clothing rods, that since one is careful about them, he sets aside a fixed place for them. So here too, one sets aside a fixed place for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה drops his first answer and gives a better one, based on a teaching of רב. The עלי is a special tool that the owner keeps in a fixed place, so it is different from an ordinary כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב taught that when an owner is very careful about a tool, he gives it a fixed place and does not want it used for anything else. Everyone agrees such tools may not be moved at all. The עלי is that kind of tool, so its prohibition does not contradict רבה's general rule about ordinary כלים שמלאכתן לאיסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Clothing rods / rollers used by launderers
He is careful / particular about it
He sets aside a fixed place for them

steps.whatToRemember: An ordinary כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved for its use (רבה). A special tool that the owner is careful about and keeps in a fixed place may not be moved, and everyone agrees about that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a separate group of tools inside the larger category of כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור. Tools the owner is careful about follow a stricter rule. Later פוסקים call this כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור שמקפיד עליו (a tool the owner is careful about).

phrases.english: Once he heard this teaching
phrases.notes: Tells us רבה changed his mind.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Chinana bar Shelamya said in the name of Rav:
Everyone agrees about launderers' pins, presses, and clothing rods
that since one is careful about them,
he sets aside a fixed place for them (so they may not be moved).
Here too (the עלי), one sets aside a fixed place for them.
phrases.notes: Applies רב's rule to the case of step 4.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּשַׁמְעַהּ לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first idea of step 5 with a better answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a tool the owner is careful about (מקפיד) is an exception to the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the עלי may not be moved, maybe no כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved for its use.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עלי is a tool the owner is careful about and keeps in a fixed place, so it is forbidden even according to everyone. רבה's rule still stands for ordinary tools.

steps.title: Dispute: which hammer did the משנה allow for cracking nuts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה's hammer is a goldsmiths' hammer. רב שמן בר אבא says it is a spice merchants' hammer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: we learned this about a goldsmiths' hammer. רב שמן בר אבא said: we learned this about a spice merchants' hammer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement between אמוראים about the משנה's hammer used to crack nuts. Each one says which kind of hammer the משנה had in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question connects to the idea of being careful about a tool from step 6. A goldsmith wants his hammer kept smooth. A spice merchant does not want his hammer to pick up other smells. The argument is about which owner is less careful, so that his hammer may be used for nuts.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)

phrases.english: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
It was about a goldsmiths' hammer that we learned (the משנה).
Rav Shemen bar Abba said:
It was about a spice merchants' hammer that we learned (the משנה).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the idea of being careful about a tool (step 6), the גמרא asks which hammer in the משנה fits that idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether the משנה's nut-cracking hammer is a goldsmiths' hammer (רבי יוחנן) or a spice merchants' hammer (רב שמן בר אבא).

steps.title: Explaining the logic of each side in the hammer dispute
steps.stepSummary: The one who allows a spice merchants' hammer surely allows a goldsmiths' hammer. The one who allows only a goldsmiths' hammer holds that a spice merchant is careful about his hammer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said a spice merchants' hammer is allowed would surely allow a goldsmiths' hammer. The one who said a goldsmiths' hammer is allowed holds that a spice merchant is careful about his hammer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how far each opinion reaches. It shows where the two opinions agree and where they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a goldsmiths' hammer may be used. They disagree only about the spice merchant. רבי יוחנן holds that the spice merchant is careful about his hammer, so it will not absorb other smells, and therefore it falls under the rule of step 6. רב שמן בר אבא allows even the spice merchants' hammer, so the goldsmiths' hammer, which is less of a concern, is surely allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a goldsmiths' hammer may be used. The argument is only whether a spice merchant is so careful about his hammer that it becomes off-limits.

phrases.english: The one who said (it is) of spice merchants,
all the more so (he allows) that of goldsmiths.
The one who said (it is) of goldsmiths —
but that of spice merchants, one is careful about it.
phrases.notes: The spice merchant does not want foreign smells absorbed into his hammer.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר דְּבַשָּׂמִים כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּזֶהָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two opinions in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goldsmiths' hammer is allowed by everyone. Whether a spice merchants' hammer is allowed depends on whether the merchant is careful about it.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the reed and the shuttle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about a reed and a shuttle, to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the reed and the shuttle" etc. (from the משנה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה to start a new discussion. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows moving a reed or a shuttle to stick it into food. Sticking a stick into food suggests food that is hidden or buried. That leads into the ברייתא about food buried in straw or coals.

phrases.english: "And the reed and the shuttle" etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה allows moving a reed or a shuttle (to stick into food).

steps.title: A buried fig or cake may be moved only if part of it is showing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an unripe fig buried in straw, or a cake buried in coals, may be moved on שבת only if part of it is uncovered.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: an unripe fig that one buried in straw, and a cake that one buried in coals: if part of it is uncovered, it may be moved. If not, it may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about food hidden inside straw or coals. It may be taken out only if part of it is showing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straw and coals are מוקצה. If part of the food is showing, you can take hold of it directly and pull it out, and the מוקצה just slides off. If it is fully covered, you would have to move the מוקצה itself to reach it, so it is forbidden. This explains why the משנה needed a reed or shuttle to stick into such food.
steps.confusionAlert: The food itself is not מוקצה. The problem is only the straw or coals covering it, which would have to be moved to get it out.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
An unripe fig that one buried in straw (to ripen it)
and a cake that one buried in coals,
if part of it is uncovered —
it is permitted to move it;
and if not — it is forbidden to move it.
phrases.notes: Because the מוקצה straw or coals would have to be moved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא connected to the משנה line about sticking a reed or shuttle into food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food buried in מוקצה (straw or coals) may be moved only if part of it is uncovered. If it is fully covered, it may not be moved.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן תדאי: Poke It With a Reed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן תדאי says you may stick a reed or a shuttle into the buried fig or cake, and the straw or coals fall off by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן תדאי says: You may stick them onto a reed or a shuttle, and the straw and coals shake off on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the ברייתא from step 10. רבי אלעזר בן תדאי adds a more lenient option: even if the fig or cake is fully covered, you may poke it out with a tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion required part of the food to be uncovered, so that you take the food without touching the מוקצה straw or coals. רבי אלעזר בן תדאי allows spearing the food with a tool even though the straw or coals get moved as a side effect. In his view, this indirect movement is not a forbidden act of moving.

keyTerms.meaning: he sticks/inserts them (pokes the food onto a tool)
a spindle or reed used in spinning

steps.confusionAlert: The food itself is not מוקצה. The problem is the straw or coals on top of it. The whole question is whether moving them indirectly counts as moving them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Tadai says:
He sticks them onto a spindle-reed or a shuttle,
and they (the straw/coals) are shaken off by themselves.
phrases.notes: The coals or straw fall away without being handled directly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second, more lenient opinion in the same ברייתא quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may spear buried food with a tool even if fully covered; the מוקצה falls off by itself.

steps.title: רב נחמן Rules Like רבי אלעזר בן תדאי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן תדאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The הלכה is like רבי אלעזר בן תדאי!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a practical ruling: we follow the lenient view of רבי אלעזר בן תדאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By ruling this way, רב נחמן seems to accept the idea behind it: moving מוקצה indirectly, as a side effect, is not real moving. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא whose rulings are often followed

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Elazar ben Tadai!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן תַּדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the dispute in steps 10-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן תדאי: spearing the buried food is allowed.

steps.title: Contradiction From רב נחמן's Radish Ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב נחמן really holds that indirect moving is allowed. In another ruling about a buried radish, he seems to forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean רב נחמן holds that moving something indirectly is not called moving? But רב נחמן said: This radish, if it was buried top-to-bottom, is permitted; if bottom-to-top, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two rulings of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A radish is buried in dirt, which is מוקצה. If the thick part is on top, pulling it up does not push the dirt, so it is allowed. If the thick part is at the bottom, pulling it up pushes the dirt aside, so רב נחמן forbids it. That means indirect moving of the dirt is forbidden, which clashes with his ruling like רבי אלעזר בן תדאי.

keyTerms.meaning: moving something indirectly / as a side effect
is this to say that...? (opening a challenge)
but didn't he say...? (introducing a contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: Top-to-bottom means the wide part is near the surface. Pulling it out does not disturb the dirt. Bottom-to-top means the wide part is deep, so the dirt gets pushed aside on the way out.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rav Nachman holds
moving from the side (indirectly)
is not called moving?
But didn't Rav Nachman say:
This radish (buried in dirt),
if wide on top, narrow below, it is permitted,
phrases.notes: No dirt is pushed when it is pulled out.

phrases.english: if wide below, narrow on top, it is forbidden!
phrases.notes: Pulling it out pushes the מוקצה dirt aside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in step 12 using another ruling of his own.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling like רבי אלעזר בן תדאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The radish ruling forbids moving dirt as a side effect, so רב נחמן seems to hold טלטול מן הצד is real moving, contradicting his lenient ruling.

steps.title: רב נחמן Retracted the Radish Ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן changed his mind about the radish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן retracted from that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: רב נחמן took back his strict radish ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rulings really do conflict. The answer is that the radish ruling was dropped, so רב נחמן's final view is that indirect moving is not forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's final position: טלטול מן הצד is not considered moving. So you may spear buried food even though the מוקצה shifts, and he retracted the strict radish ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the הלכה for indirectly moving מוקצה for the sake of something permitted.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman retracted
from that (radish ruling).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: one of the conflicting statements was withdrawn
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן held both rulings at once, so his view on indirect moving is unclear.
steps.terutzMaskana: He abandoned the radish ruling; his final view is that indirect moving is permitted.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: The Hand Needle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about a hand needle used to take out a thorn.
steps.simpleTranslation: A hand needle, to take out with it, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This is a setup line that opens the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows moving an ordinary sewing needle on שבת to remove a thorn. The next step asks what happens if the needle is damaged.

keyTerms.meaning: etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.aramaic: מַחַט שֶׁל יָד לִיטּוֹל בָּהּ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: A hand needle, to take out (a thorn) with it, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, after finishing the buried-food discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hand needle may be moved on שבת to remove a thorn.

steps.title: What About a Needle Missing Its Eye or Point?
steps.stepSummary: רבא בריה דרבה asks רב יוסף whether a needle whose eye or point broke off may be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא son of רבה sent to רב יוסף: Let our teacher teach us: A needle whose eye or point was removed, what is its status?
steps.whatsHappening: A student sends a practical question to his teacher about a broken needle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A needle without an eye can no longer sew, and one without a point is damaged too. The question is whether it is still a כלי that may be moved, or whether it became broken junk that is מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: let our teacher teach us (a respectful way of asking)
its eye (the hole of the needle)

phrases.english: Rava son of Rabba sent (a question)
to Rav Yosef:
Let our teacher teach us,
a needle whose eye or point was removed,
what is its status (may it be moved)?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה לְרַב יוֹסֵף יְלַמְּדֵנוּ רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a damaged version of the needle in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a needle missing its eye or point keeps its status as a כלי that may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: The Thorn Doesn't Care About the Eye
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers from the משנה: a needle is allowed for removing a thorn, and a thorn does not care whether the needle has an eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You learned it already: A hand needle, to take out a thorn with it. And what does the thorn care whether it has a hole or doesn't have a hole?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tells the student that the answer is already in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows the needle because it can remove a thorn, not because it can sew. Removing a thorn does not need the eye, so a needle without an eye is still useful and may be moved. His argument from the משנה directly addresses the missing eye.

keyTerms.meaning: does it matter to it / does it care

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי keeps its permitted status on שבת as long as it is still fit for a use the משנה recognizes. A needle without an eye can still remove a thorn.

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it (already):
A hand needle
to take out a thorn with it:
And what does the thorn care
whether it (the needle) is pierced or not pierced?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 using the משנה quoted in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A needle without an eye may be moved, since the משנה permits it for removing a thorn, which does not need the eye.

steps.title: Challenge from the law of a broken needle in טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבא בריה דרבה challenges רב יוסף from a משנה: a needle whose eye or point was removed becomes טהורה, so it is no longer a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: a needle whose eye or point was removed becomes pure, doesn't it?
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner pushes back on רב יוסף's answer using a source from the laws of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken object can no longer hold טומאה, so a needle that becomes טהורה once its eye or point is gone is clearly no longer a כלי. If it is not a כלי, why would it be permitted to move on שבת? The challenge assumes that the definition of a כלי is the same in both areas of law.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from a source)
Its eye (the hole of the needle)
Pure, meaning it cannot hold טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Here טהורה does not mean 'clean' in a good sense. It means the needle is too broken to count as a כלי, so it cannot hold טומאה.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רבא בריה דרבה challenges רב יוסף.

phrases.english: A needle whose eye was removed
or its point — is pure?
phrases.notes: Pure means it is no longer a כלי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that a needle missing its eye or point may be moved on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For טומאה, such a needle is not a כלי. A non-כלי should not be movable on שבת.

steps.title: אביי: טומאה and שבת use different standards
steps.stepSummary: אביי defends רב יוסף: טומאה requires a working כלי, while שבת only requires something usable, and the broken needle can still remove a thorn.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Are you comparing טומאה to שבת? For טומאה we need a functional working utensil. For שבת we need something that is usable, and this needle is still usable for removing a thorn.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by saying you cannot learn שבת from טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי splits the definition of a כלי into two different tests. טומאה asks whether the item is a complete working utensil, and the broken needle fails that test. שבת only asks whether the item is useful for something, and the needle passes because it can still remove a thorn.

keyTerms.meaning: You are contrasting / raising a contradiction
Something that is fit for use

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key question for the rest of the sugya: does the word כלי mean the same thing in טומאה and in שבת?

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Are you contrasting impurity with Shabbat?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: the two areas of law are different.

phrases.english: For impurity, we require a functional utensil;
regarding Shabbat, we require something that is fit for use —
and this one too is fit
to take out a thorn with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18 on behalf of רב יוסף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two areas of law (טומאה versus שבת).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenger assumed that 'not a כלי for טומאה' means 'not a כלי for שבת.'
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת only needs usability, so the broken needle still counts for moving.

steps.title: רבא: The challenge is correct
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's distinction: if the needle is not a כלי for טומאה, it is not a כלי for שבת either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The one who raised the challenge raised a good challenge. Since it is not a כלי for טומאה, it is also not a כלי for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sides with the challenger and rejects אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that there is only one definition of a כלי. A needle that lost its כלי status for טומאה lost it for שבת too. That would mean it may not be moved, which goes against רב יוסף's ruling.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The one who objects, objects well.
Since regarding impurity it is not a utensil —

phrases.aramaic: לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת נָמֵי לָאו מָנָא הוּא.
phrases.english: regarding Shabbat it is also not a utensil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer in Step 19 and restores the challenge from Step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's distinction between טומאה and שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is one definition of a כלי. Losing that status for טומאה means losing it for שבת too.

steps.title: A ברייתא separates שבת from טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from a ברייתא: a needle may be moved on שבת whether or not it has an eye, and the eye only matters for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A needle, whether it has a hole or not, may be moved on שבת. The rule about the hole was said only for טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to go directly against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly says that the needle's eye matters only for טומאה, not for שבת. This is exactly אביי's distinction, so רבא's claim that both areas use one standard seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
Perforated, meaning it has an eye or hole

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge targets רבא, not רב יוסף. The ברייתא actually supports רב יוסף and אביי.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מַחַט, בֵּין נְקוּבָה בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָהּ נְקוּבָה —
phrases.english: A needle, whether perforated or not perforated —
it is permitted to move it on Shabbat.
And they did not speak of 'perforated'
except regarding impurity alone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's position from Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the definition of a כלי is the same for שבת and for טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the eye matters only for טומאה and allows moving the needle on שבת either way, so the two areas use different standards.

steps.title: אביי explains the ברייתא according to רבא: it is about unfinished needles
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the challenge against רבא. The ברייתא's needle 'without an eye' is an unfinished needle that was never pierced. A finished needle whose eye or point broke off is thrown out as junk.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי explained the ברייתא according to רבא: we are dealing with unfinished needles. Sometimes a person decides to use them as they are and makes them a utensil. But when a finished needle's eye or point was removed, a person throws it among the junk.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from the ברייתא in step 21 and shows that the ברייתא does not contradict רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a needle may be moved on שבת 'whether or not it has an eye.' אביי says this refers to a needle that was never pierced. A person might choose to use it as it is, so it counts as a כלי. A needle that was finished and then lost its eye or point is broken. People throw it away, so רבא's ruling still stands: it is not a כלי for טומאה or for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it / interpreted it (usually explaining a source so it fits a certain view)
Unfinished items, raw forms (here: needles not yet pierced)

steps.whatToRemember: An unfinished needle that was never pierced can still count as a כלי, because a person may choose to use it as it is. A finished needle that broke is junk and is not a כלי, neither for טומאה nor for שבת (רבא's view).
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not giving his own opinion here. In step 20 רבא rejected אביי's distinction. Even so, אביי now explains the ברייתא so that it fits רבא's view. The גמרא often does this: a sage explains how a source works for a view he himself does not hold.

phrases.english: Abaye interpreted it according to Rava:
phrases.notes: אביי explains the ברייתא from step 21 so that it fits רבא's view.

phrases.english: we are dealing with unfinished (needles),
phrases.notes: These are needles whose eye was never pierced.

phrases.english: sometimes one decides about them,
and makes them into a utensil.
phrases.notes: He decides to use them as they are, without piercing them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּנִיטַּל חֲרָרָהּ אוֹ עוּקְצָהּ —
phrases.english: But where its eye or its point was removed —
phrases.notes: This means a finished needle that later broke.

phrases.english: a person throws it among the junk.
phrases.notes: Since people throw it away, it has lost its status as a כלי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא (step 21) against רבא's position (step 20).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is set in a different case, unfinished needles.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that any needle without an eye, even a broken one, may be moved on שבת, which would contradict רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about unfinished needles that a person may decide to use as they are. Broken finished needles are junk, just as רבא said.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about straightening a baby's limbs on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins: may one straighten the limbs of a baby on שבת? רב נחמן forbids it and רב ששת permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding straightening the limbs of a baby: רב נחמן forbids it, and רב ששת permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the needle topic and opens a new question. It records a מחלוקת between רב נחמן and רב ששת about straightening a baby's limbs on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straightening a baby's limbs means setting them into their proper shape. רב נחמן worries that this looks like 'fixing' something into its finished form, which resembles a forbidden מלאכה. רב ששת sees no problem and permits it.

phrases.english: Straightening (the limbs of) an infant —
phrases.notes: This is the topic heading for the new discussion.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman prohibits,
and Rav Sheshet permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַסּוֹבֵי יָנוֹקָא — רַב נַחְמָן אָסַר, וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת שָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The needle discussion has ended. This step opens a new topic about fixing or shaping on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: רב נחמן forbids straightening a baby's limbs on שבת, and רב ששת permits it.

steps.title: רב נחמן begins to bring a source from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן starts to prove his view that it is forbidden. He opens with 'from where do I say this?' and begins quoting a משנה: 'One may not make...'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: From where do I say this? As we learned in a משנה: One may not make...
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן begins to bring a proof from a משנה for his ruling. The quote continues on the next amud, so this step sets up the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'מנא אמינא לה' signals that a sage is about to support his own ruling with a source. The משנה he starts quoting lists things one may not do on שבת. He will use it to show that straightening a baby is forbidden. The full proof only becomes clear once the quote is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (a sage introducing proof for his own view)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: This is the standard opening when a sage proves his own ruling.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: One may not make
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן begins to support his ruling (forbidding) from step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that straightening a baby's limbs on שבת is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה beginning 'אין עושין' (the quote continues on the next amud).
